51543436.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to CM5 chip immobilised recombinant mouse perforin expressed in baculovirus-infected Sf21 cells by SPR analysis
51543436.references_previous: S.S. Lim, C.O. Debono, C.A. MacRaid, I.R. Chandrashekar, O. Dolezal, R. F. Anders, J.S. Simpson, M.J. Scanlon, P.J. Devine, S. Scammells, R.S. Norton, Development of inhibitors of Plasmodium falciparum apical membrane antigen 1 based on fragment screening, Aust. J. Chem. 66 (2013) 1530–1536.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 4.3. Surface pla: A Biacore T200 biosensor was employed to estimate binding affinities. mPerforin was immobilised on a CM5 sensor chip using an amine-coupling methodology similar to that described previously [40]. Approximately 8000 RU of protein was coupled in a single flow cell (1000 RU = 1 ng of protein per mm²). A reference flow cell on the same chip was prepared by subjecting it to the identical amine coupling procedure with no protein being injected. All SPR binding experiments were conducted at 25 °C with 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% P20, as the running buffer at a constant flow rate of 60 mL min⁻¹. Immobilised mPerforin was equilibrated with 30 s blank buffer injections of 30 s contact time before the start of the binding experiments. Solvent correction curves were obtained from a series of injections of running buffer containing 4.55–5.95% (v/v) DMSO. Fragment samples and elaborated molecules were typically screened at concentrations ranging from 6.25 to 200 μM, with 30 s contact times. All binding data were processed and analysed using Biacore T200 evaluation software version 1.0. The binding affinities of fragment hits were estimated based on the response (RU) from six different concentrations with a fixed fragment Rmax (maximal binding capacity of the protein surface).
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Fig. 5. Lipid SPR. (A) Schematic showing SPR experimental design. (B) Correlation of K_D values with KHYG-1 potency. (C) Affinity fit for 4 binding to mPerforin on CM5 and L1 chips [20 mM HEPES (pH 7.4), 150 mM NaCl, 2 mM CaCl₂, 0.5% DMSO]. (D) Affinity fit for 5 binding to a mPerforin on CM5 and L1 chips [20 mM HEPES (pH 7.4), 150 mM NaCl, 2 mM CaCl₂, 0.5% DMSO].
original_paragraph.Figure 5C and 5D sensorgrams: Figure 5C shows sensorgrams for compound 4 binding to mPerforin on CM5 (amine coupled) and L1 (lipid) chips. The x-axis for CM5 is labeled '4 (nM)' with a range from 0 to 30000. The x-axis for L1 is labeled '4 (nM)' with a range from 0 to 1500. Figure 5D shows sensorgrams for compound 5 binding to mPerforin on CM5 and L1 chips. The x-axis for CM5 is labeled '5 (nM)' with a range from 0 to 30000. The x-axis for L1 is labeled '5 (nM)' with a range from 0 to 1500. The y-axis for all plots is labeled 'R.U.' (Response Units).
original_paragraph.Results section - SPR affinities: SPR affinities measured using lipid-immobilised mPerforin also correlated better with potencies measured in the KHYG-1 assay than those measured using covalently-immobilised perforin (Fig. 5B). As perforin adopts a specific orientation at the target cell membrane during pore formation, one explanation is that lipid-based immobilisation is likely to be a more faithful recapitulation of the native conformation than amine coupling, which immobilises perforin in random orientations on the SPR chip surface.

assay_conditions.running_buffer_composition: 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% P20
